Amblyopia, also known as lazy eye, is a condition where there is a reduction or loss of vision in one eye. However, the visual loss associated with amblyopia is not always permanent. 

In some cases, older individuals with a history of amblyopia who experience visual loss in their previously normal eye may see an improvement in visual function in the amblyopic eye over time. This recovery of visual function can occur after the loss of vision in the fellow eye and may be sustained. 

It's essential to note that the extent of recovery can vary, and the likelihood of improvement may depend on several factors, including the severity of the amblyopia and the individual's overall eye health. If you have concerns about amblyopia or are experiencing visual loss, it's crucial to consult with an eye care professional for personalized advice and treatment.
